axes: Roblox (x, y, z) = Blender (x, z, -y); asset front = Roblox LookVector (-Z); base on y = 0
tangentSpace: MikkTSpace tangents exported (glTF TANGENT on every primitive, checked after export); normal maps are OpenGL (+Y), tangent space
import: Geometry: import each GLB (3D Importer / Open Cloud Model). Every asset root arrives as a Model of MeshParts named <Asset>_<Role>[_n]; re-centre with the asset 'origin' (WorldPivot = CFrame.new(origin), then PivotTo) exactly like the other categories. The meshes carry tangents, so normal maps work.

Surfaces: give every part ONE SurfaceAppearance built from its 'surfaceAppearance' block: ColorMap / NormalMap / RoughnessMap = the uploaded image ids of those PNG files (each file once - 14 images in total, shared by every asset; RoughnessMap uses the separate 8-bit grayscale TR_Rough_*.png), MetalnessMap empty (nothing is metal), AlphaMode as given, Color = 'color' (sRGB tint; it multiplies the ColorMap - the species differ only by these tints, so never skip it). Do not rely on the importer's auto SurfaceAppearance for roughness: the GLB packs roughness into a glTF metallicRoughness image (glb_only/*_MR.png, metallicFactor 0). Clear any importer-created TextureID.

Cards (backFacesInMesh = true) already contain flipped back faces: keep MeshPart.DoubleSided = false (otherwise the back sides z-fight) and MeshPart.Transparency = 0 so AlphaMode Transparency is an alpha cut-out (no sorting). Each alpha part says so in its 'alphaSetup'.

Per part: CanCollide = collide, CollisionFidelity = collision, CastShadow = castShadow, CanQuery = canQuery, CanTouch = canTouch, Anchored = true; Material = robloxMaterial (physics/sounds only, the look comes from the SurfaceAppearance); 'rgb' is a fallback MeshPart.Color matching the texture.
OakA: OakA_Bark gets the CollectionService tag Climbable; attachments Perch1..N as in the v1 oaks.

Check in Studio: card shadows should be cut out (dappled); if a crown casts solid card-shaped shadows, set CastShadow = false on that Foliage part. RenderFidelity Automatic is fine; if far crowns break up, use Precise on Foliage parts.

parts.alphaSetup: SurfaceAppearance.AlphaMode = Transparency with MeshPart.Transparency = 0 (alpha-tested cut-out: depth-correct, no sorting) and MeshPart.DoubleSided = false - the back faces are real, flipped duplicate faces in the mesh
